commentary: The GPU rental waterfall shows sharp compression: B200 at $7 typical is only ~2.8x the H100 floor ($2.50 typical), while H100-to-A100 spread has collapsed to ~1.7x, signaling oversupply in prior-gen and rational pricing discipline as Blackwell ramps. Depreciation disclosures create a $176B accounting gap through 2028—Amazon's reversal to 5-year life directly contradicts the 6-year schedules at MSFT/GOOGL/ORCL/META, exposing the risk that faster GPU obsolescence forces a profit reset if the others follow. CoreWeave's credit deterioration (CDS at 50% default odds, spreads widening 325bps in four months despite investment-grade debt) signals the market is repricing GPU collateral value downward faster than the accounting, which directly pressures the entire rental-rate curve if lenders demand higher returns or tighter LTVs on future financings.
